A1.justification: Both PDFs describe 3D-Prover. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original transition-prediction experiments, miniF2F proof-search results, ablations and embedding analyses in Sections 2–3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds InternLM experiments, LeanDojo evaluation, subgoal-diversity measurements and computational analyses.

M1.justification: v1 Appendix A.4 only suggests separately embedding the goal. v2 Section 2.2 implements COMBINED (SMALL GOAL), supplying a single goal vector to the tactic encoder, and uses it with InternLM. This is a limited architectural extension; the transition objectives, quality scoring and k-DPP filtering remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix D adds training and evaluation on LeanDojo Novel Premises, comprising 2,000 evaluation goals, alongside the retained miniF2F benchmarks. This introduces a separate proof population; v1 used LeanDojo tooling but did not report this benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: The principal comparator addition is No Filtering, newly reported for the existing ReProver experiments and additional evaluations. Table 3 compares InternLM-based 3D-Prover against Top-K under best-first search and No Filtering under critic-guided search. The earlier Top-K, Random, Autoencoder and transition-model controls remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 7B InternLM setup using temperature-0.7 sampling, 128 initial samples deduplicated to at most 64 candidates, K=8 filtering, and best-first or critic-guided search. Its transition model trains on miniF2F-test transitions, unlike the retained ReProver valid-to-test setup. New analyses introduce shortest-observed-proof-length normalization and subgoal similarity measured with all-MiniLM-L6-v2.

E4.justification: v2 adds the compact-goal architectural comparison, proof-length analysis on LeanDojo, similarity analysis of resulting subgoal text, and InternLM candidate-count analysis. It also replaces the rough overhead discussion with measured timing and memory comparisons. The original tactic-embedding analyses and hyperparameter sweep are retained; v1 Table 5 is relocated to v2 Table 12.

E5.justification: Table 2 changes from mean plus standard error to mean with minimum and maximum. Both versions specify four ReProver runs, without stating an increase. v2 additionally documents two- and six-attempt InternLM evaluations and standard deviations for computational measurements; existing tactic-level standard-error reporting remains.

E6.justification: New results include InternLM best-first Pass@1 of 45.7% versus 44.3% for Top-K (Table 3), LeanDojo Pass@1 of 32.3% versus 31.3% for Top-K (Table 11), and compact-goal, intermediate Pass@k and subgoal-similarity results. Original ReProver mean proof rates and most ablation values remain unchanged. The new 0.9% timing and approximately 7% memory overhead measurements concern InternLM, so they are not a matched-setting improvement over v1's roughly doubled ReProver generation time.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2.1 corrects the transition model's status-output codomain from {0,1} to [0,1], consistent with its probability-valued predictor. The proof-search formalism, training-loss mathematics and DPP framework are otherwise substantively retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the claimed demonstrated applicability from ReProver on miniF2F to multiple proving LLMs and the LeanDojo benchmark. The central contributions—learning transition-aware representations and using DPP filtering to improve proof search—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the costly, unbatchable-overhead account with an efficiency interpretation based on the new InternLM setup. It adds interpretations of proof-length and subgoal-diversity evidence, frames same-dataset adaptation as online improvement, and explicitly discusses restricted evaluation scale, including single-run LeanDojo results. Conversely, it removes v1's warning that transition-training and test splits can contain the same goals.

D1.justification: v2 provides an explicit code-repository link and substantially expands reproducibility information. Appendices G–I document sampling and deduplication, filtering time and VRAM usage, evaluation GPUs and CPUs, concurrent provers, training and evaluation durations, run totals and compute estimates. These are largely new disclosures; the original optimizer, learning rate, batch size and epoch settings remain.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces its extensive catalogue of proving papers with Li et al.'s survey, removing numerous individual references. v2 adds InternLM, DPP application references and CARTS, explicitly distinguishing its pre-execution filtering from CARTS's subgoal selection after execution. Section 2.2 also strengthens novelty positioning by claiming the first demonstration of learning proof-system dynamics.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: proof-search preliminaries move to Appendix A, DPP background moves from Section 3 to Section 1.2, and the model explanation is rewritten with simpler indexing. The conclusion replaces future-work discussion with limitations, while the appendices are reorganized into separately named sections.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography, title and author layout, caption placement and algorithm formatting. Table 2 stacks the two benchmarks instead of placing them side by side, and the Autoencoder comparison is transposed. Existing diagrams are resized, the environment-response table moves to the appendix, and new experimental tables and the candidate-count histogram expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow evidence for general applicability and practical cost through a second prover, another proof dataset, direct proof-length and subgoal-diversity analyses, an implemented compact-goal variant, and fuller reproducibility documentation. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: InternLM uses training transitions from its evaluation benchmark, LeanDojo results have limited replication, and the split-dependence caveat disappears. There is also a new inconsistency: Table 9 reports Random K=16 Pass@1 as 21.2%, outside Table 2's 24.5–25.7% range. Efficiency measurements use different configurations and therefore do not establish a matched-setting speedup.
